newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end higher in subdued trade before FOMC meet.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end higher in subdued trade before FOMC meet.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures closed higher on Monday on dealer short-covering, market sources said.

Support was provided by continued rolling forward of short positions to September ahead of a benchmark shift, the yen's rise against the dollar after Japan's April trade data and scattered cash bond buying from investors, traders said.
They said activity was subdued, however, ahead of Tuesday's U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.
"The cash market was very quiet ahead of the FOMC meeting tomorrow," said a dealer at a trust bank's securities unit.
June JGBs ended at 124.40, up 0.42 from Friday's finish. Turnover was 41,926 contracts.

June rose from the opening as the yen strengthened versus the dollar due to a sharp rise in Japan's April customs-cleared trade surplus, traders said. They added, however, that selling pressure on the June contract increased when it neared 124.50, which became a solid ceiling.
The finance ministry said Japan's trade surplus more than doubled in April from a year earlier to 831.48 billion yen.
The dollar slipped below 115 yen after the release of the trade data, against Friday's New York close at 115.65/75.

"Those who had expected the yen's rise and weakness in Tokyo stocks took long positions this morning. But these positions were quickly liquidated as the Nikkei posted healthy gains," the dealer said. The Nikkei 225 average ended Monday at a new high for the calendar year, rising 165.02 points or 0.81 percent to 20,489.75.
There was market talk that a U.S. hedge fund was rolling forward short positions from June to the September contract, said a foreign bank trader.
Others said scattered buying was detected in cash bonds this morning and this triggered stop-loss buying by dealers.
June rose as high as 124.47 before easing when the Nikkei average extended its gains in the afternoon.
Some traders said a European hedge fund was among buyers of cash bonds this morning. The foreign bank trader said the fund was buying cash JGBs from the 111th to the 129th issues.
Elsewhere in cash bonds, a dealer at a long-term credit bank's securities unit said profit-taking sales were seen in the intermediate zone of the JGB yield curve.
"I see the JGB market remaining caught in a range between the price-of-par levels for 2.8 percent 10-year JGBs and 2.6 percent 10-year JGBs," the dealer said.
That is equivalent to the key June contract moving between slightly above 123.00 and just below 125.00, he said.
Views were divided on whether U.S. interest rates will be raised on Tuesday. Another factor keeping investors mostly away was a 10-year JGB auction expected on Wednesday, traders said.
Some said if U.S. interest rates are raised by 0.25 point, that may dampen JGBs.

"If Tokyo stocks rise following the Dow Industrial Index's welcoming the Fed's tightening, the June may fall below its recent low of 122.70," a dealer at a city bank's securities unit said. -- Risa Maeda Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
